findings.text: Bribery is illegal under US law extra-territorially and under the laws the OECD conventions have prompted; the text credits the OECD Convention on Combating Bribery of Foreign Public Officials with forty-three signatories.
findings.problem: The plural 'OECD conventions' credits both conventions with prompting national laws. The source (and the repaired deep ref) credits only the 1997 OECD Anti-Bribery Convention with getting its signatories to enact stricter laws; the separately named Convention on Combating Bribery is given only its forty-three signatories. The 1997 convention is also left unnamed, so the two instruments blur again.
findings.evidence: Source 11447-11453: 'The 1997 Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) Anti-Bribery Convention has been instrumental in getting its signatories (the United Kingdom and most European Union nations) to enact stricter antibribery laws... There is also the OECD Convention on Combating Bribery of Foreign Public Officials in International Business Transactions, which has forty-three signatories'. Deep 304.
findings.fix: correct: Bribery is illegal under US law extra-territorially and under the stricter laws the 1997 OECD Anti-Bribery Convention has pushed its signatories to enact; the text separately credits the OECD Convention on Combating Bribery of Foreign Public Officials in International Business Transactions with forty-three signatories.
